Non-Profit - Statewide
The United Voice For Active Outdoor Recreationists
4264 EAST FLORENCE AVENUE BELL, CALIFORNIA 90201 AREA CODE 213 - 773-6260 AREA CODE 213 - 585-0581
June 22, 1972
Department of the Interior Office of the Secretary Washington, D.C. 20240
Gentlemen:
We have the letter of June 14 from Deputy Assistant Secretary Lyons together with enclosures, and we appreciate the opportunity to comment on the Draft Environmental Statement (DES) proposed for Departmental implementation of Executive Order 11644.
We have reviewed the Off-Road Recreation Vehicle Task Force Study Report of March 15, 1972 (ORRV), and we find that the differences between that thorough study, for which we would compliment the Department and those who prepared it, and the DES difficult to reconcile.
The entire thrust of the ORRV Report is that the off-road vehicle user has a right to use and enjoy the public lands of this nation; the Report specifically recognizes the great lack of factual information (pp 42 et seq & 69, and Recommendation 8, p. 73); it specifically recommends that off-road vehicle use be recognized as an accepted recreational use and that existing use areas be kept open to the public "... where environmental balance is not at issue." (Recommendation 3, p. 70)
We would compliment the Department on this position that, in view of the need for additional study, governmental regulation should not rush blindly into the vacuum of its own ignorance with restrictions for which there is no evidence of need. We think that this is in accord with a fundamental tenet of this nation's legal system: we do not presume ever anyone's guilt.
The promise to the ear, though, was apparently only to be broken to the hope, for what was so doubtful in March evidently had become certain by May when the DES was issued. The DES could easily have been prepared without any assistance from the ORRV Report; in fact only one of the ORRV Report recommendations is included in the DES (#5), and that one is a purely restrictive one.
